page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmr5s.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server configuration designed for large-scale enterprise applications requiring significant memory capacity per core. Operating on x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, the server is powered by Intel Xeon 8163 processors running at a base clock speed of 2.5 GHz. It provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs paired with 768 GB of system memory, yielding an 8.0 GB memory-to-vCPU ratio. This high memory density supports expansive datasets directly in RAM without relying on virtual swapping mechanisms.

Networking performance is defined by a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth capacity, enabling efficient data transfer across cloud services and clustered environments. The instance does not include bundled local disk storage or dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, nor does it include complimentary public IPv4 addresses. Storage functionality relies entirely on external network storage solutions, which decouples storage scaling from compute and memory resources.

From an architectural and qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.ebmr5s.24xlarge provides maximum memory availability within a single node, avoiding extra expense for unused local storage or accelerator hardware. Tradeoffs include full reliance on network storage latency and bandwidth for persistent write operations. This configuration fits enterprise workloads such as in-memory databases, real-time analytics engines, big data processing pipelines, enterprise resource planning (ERP) deployments, and memory-intensive caching layers.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.ebmr5s.24xlarge is a memory-optimized server configuration designed for data-intensive enterprise workloads. Built on x86_64 architecture with the KVM hypervisor, it features 96 dedicated vCPUs powered by Intel Xeon 8163 processors clocked at 2.5 GHz. The instance offers 768 GB of total memory, maintaining an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound operations. Network connectivity is supported by a 32 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The server includes no local NVMe storage and no discrete GPUs, requiring external network-attached storage for persistence. This hardware layout provides high memory density without the overhead of attached local disks, delivering qualitative cost efficiency for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, data processing pipelines, and memory-heavy transactional applications.
